219.name: 17th Street Bicycle Safety Project
219.teaser: Working to improve safety for all road users on 17th Street between Church and Sanchez
219.summary: On 17th Street between Church and Sanchez, "People on bicycles are being injured in falls" on the streetcar tracks and poor pavement. Past fixes had not stopped the crashes, and "people with disabilities are having a difficult time crossing the street."

381.name: Folsom-Howard Streetscape Project
381.teaser: Improving Transportation Safety and Access in SoMa
381.summary: Folsom and Howard are three- and four-lane one-way arterials "designed for trucks and cars serving the manufacturing and warehousing industry". With SoMa's growth in housing and jobs, the page says "Walkways and bikeways are currently inadequate", and the project rebuilds both streets for walking, biking and transit.

653.name: 7th Street and 8th Street Safety Projects
facilities: 0.1 mi signed route on a calm street
0.1 mi painted lane on a calm street
653.teaser: Bringing quick-build traffic safety improvements to SoMa
653.summary: 7th and 8th Streets are a one-way couplet in SoMa whose design, with freeway ramps and the 19-Polk, "presents the potential for crashes between people walking, bicycling, taking transit and driving." The project brought quick-build safety changes to what the page calls "important bicycle network links" to Mission Bay and Caltrain.
upgraded: 0.1 mi signed route on a calm street
0.1 mi painted lane on a calm street

807.name: Wiggle Neighborhood Green Corridor
facilities: 0.9 mi signed route on a calm street
807.teaser: The SFMTA's goal for the Wiggle Neighborhood Green Corridor is to create a route that is comfortable and safe for all who walk, bike, and live along the Wiggle
807.summary: SFMTA, SFPUC and Public Works rebuilt the Wiggle with stormwater management and bike and pedestrian safety changes. The goal: "a route that is comfortable and safe for all who walk, bike, and live along the Wiggle".
upgraded: 0.9 mi signed route on a calm street

851.name: Turk Street Safety Project
851.summary: Turk Street between Market and Gough was chosen "based on its inclusion on the Vision Zero High Injury Network", the 13 percent of streets with 75 percent of injuries and deaths. The project added safety changes along a dense corridor of families, seniors, workers and students.

853.name: Masonic Avenue Streetscape Project
facilities: 0.2 mi painted lane on a calm street
853.summary: Masonic Avenue between Geary and Fell was on the city's Vision Zero High Injury Network. The project rebuilt it with "wider sidewalks, a new median, new paving, landscaping, raised bikeways, better lighting and upgraded sewer infrastructure."
upgraded: 0.2 mi painted lane on a calm street

939.name: Better Market Street
facilities: 0.0 mi painted lane on a calm street
upgraded: 0.0 mi painted lane on a calm street

1012.name: Division/13th Street Safety Project
1012.teaser: Improving safety, comfort, and access for people walking and biking!
1012.summary: Division and 13th Streets are "a key east-west corridor for people biking" to Caltrain, the Mission and South Beach. "In a five year period alone, there were 106 collisions along the Division/13th Street corridor, including two traffic deaths."

1032.name: Twin Peaks Figure 8 Redesign Project
1032.summary: A Recreation and Park project, with SFMTA and Public Works, on Twin Peaks Boulevard. The SFMTA and RPD "implemented the Twin Peaks Pilot Promenade" in July 2016, and the pilot configuration "was made permanent in June 2020".

1075.name: Bryant Street Bike Network Improvement Project
facilities: 0.2 mi painted lane on a calm street
1075.teaser: The SFMTA is proposing to upgrade Bryant Street between Division and 17th Streets in coordination with repaving with new bike facilities and streamlined Muni stops.
1075.summary: "The SFMTA is proposing to upgrade Bryant Street between Division and 17th Streets in coordination with repaving with new bike facilities and streamlined Muni stops."
added: 0.2 mi painted lane on a calm street

1092.name: 8th Avenue Neighborway Project
facilities: 1.6 mi signed route on a calm street
1092.summary: The goal was "a safe and pleasant north-south route for people walking and biking in the Inner Richmond." The project used "speed humps, painted markings, stop signs, and other measures" on 8th Avenue.
upgraded: 1.6 mi signed route on a calm street

1102.name: Townsend Corridor Improvement Project
1102.teaser: Improving safety and access on Townsend Street
1102.summary: Townsend Street has "one of the richest mixes of travel modes of any street in San Francisco", centered on the Caltrain station at 4th and Townsend. The project redesigned it for the thousands of people an hour who reach the station by bike, on foot, by rail and by bus.

1122.name: Vicente Street Bicycle and Pedestrian Safety Project
facilities: 1.5 mi painted lane on a calm street
1122.summary: SFMTA's summary: "Improving safety on Vicente Street". The project page text beyond that could not be read.
upgraded: 1.5 mi painted lane on a calm street

1128.name: 20th Avenue Neighborway Project
facilities: 1.7 mi painted lane on a calm street
1.3 mi signed route on a calm street
1128.teaser: Making walking and biking safer in your neighborhood
1128.summary: A north-south route through the Sunset to Golden Gate Park and Stern Grove, meant to be "a more pleasant north-south route for people walking and biking". It added "a bike lane in the uphill directions, speed cushions" and turned some angled parking to parallel. The SFMTA Board approved it on June 4, 2019.
upgraded: 1.7 mi painted lane on a calm street
1.3 mi signed route on a calm street

1134.name: Brannan Street Safety Project
facilities: 0.1 mi painted lane on a calm street
1134.teaser: Bringing safety improvements for all road users on Brannan Street
1134.summary: SFMTA's summary: "Bringing safety improvements for all road users on Brannan Street". The rest of the project page could not be read.
added: 0.1 mi painted lane on a calm street

1146.name: 5th Street Improvement Project
1146.teaser: Improving safety of all modes that travel along this corridor
1146.summary: The project "improves safety along the corridor for those who walk, bike, and drive" on 5th Street. Its first phase, the 5th Street Quick Build completed in 2020, "installed time and cost efficient, short-term upgrades"; a permanent project follows.

1202.name: Polk Streetscape Project
1202.teaser: Improving safety for all road users on Polk Street
1202.summary: Polk Street carries the 19 Polk and is "a preferred north-south bicycle route due to its flatter terrain." The streetscape project redesigned it to improve "safety for all road users on Polk Street".

1204.name: Second Street Improvement Project
1204.summary: 2nd Street from Market to King, which the East SoMa Area Plan named "a primary pedestrian, bicycle and transit thoroughfare". The project aimed at "transforming 2nd Street into a pleasant multi-modal corridor".

1267.name: Laurel Heights/Jordan Park Traffic Calming Project
facilities: 0.3 mi painted lane on a calm street
1267.summary: A traffic calming project "initiated by area residents to help reduce the negative impacts of motor vehicle traffic while improving safety and access for people walking and biking." The measures on local streets came from resident input and traffic surveys.
upgraded: 0.3 mi painted lane on a calm street

1305.name: Northbound San Jose Avenue and I-280 Off-Ramp Road Diet Pilot Project
1305.summary: The "Bernal Cut" of San Jose Avenue "hosts freeway-like conditions on a city street", partly fed by a two-lane I-280 off-ramp. The pilot narrowed it to slow vehicles and "increase safety and comfort for all road users".

2082.name: Upper Clipper Street Traffic Calming Project
2082.teaser: Improvements and paving coming to Upper Clipper Street
2082.summary: Public Works repaved Upper Clipper Street, and SFMTA used the repaving to answer "community requests for traffic calming." The chosen design "keep[s] the center turn lane and retain[s] all existing parking."

15731.name: Valencia Bikeway Improvements
15731.teaser: Making Valencia Street safer for all
15731.summary: Valencia Street "has been a key Mission District corridor in the bikeway network for more than 25 years." The project rebuilt its bikeway to improve "safety and comfort" on a street the page calls one of the country's biggest collections of independent businesses.

16577.name: Indiana Street Bikeway Project
16577.teaser: Providing a better bike connection on Indiana Street
16577.summary: Indiana Street (Bicycle Route 7) "had no bike lanes between 23rd Street to Cesar Chavez" because of one-way traffic to the I-280 on-ramp. The goal was "a safe and comfortable north-south bike route connection in the Dogpatch Neighborhood."

17131.name: Alemany Interchange Bike Lanes Project
17131.teaser: The Alemany Interchange Bike Lanes project will add protected bikeways to both directions of Alemany Boulevard through the US 101/I-280 interchange, and a southbound buffered bike lane on San Bruno from Alemany Boulevard to Silver Avenue.
17131.summary: The project "will add protected bikeways to both directions of Alemany Boulevard through the US 101/I-280 interchange", the "Alemany Maze", plus a southbound buffered bike lane on San Bruno Avenue. The page notes "No changes to parking will be made".

17912.name: Sansome and Battery Connections Project
17912.summary: The project gave people walking and biking between the Embarcadero and the Financial District "an alternative route parallel to the traffic-heavy Embarcadero corridor", with new bike lanes on Sansome and Battery. It was fully completed in December 2019.

20166.name: Howard Street Quick-Build Project
20166.teaser: Ensuring a safer travel environment for all moving along Howard Street between 3rd Street and the Embarcadero
20166.summary: On Howard Street between 3rd Street and the Embarcadero the project would "upgrade the existing bike lane to a parking-protected bike lane", add a bike signal at 3rd Street and transit boarding islands, and reduce vehicle lanes. The page says the work "is complete."

20169.name: Folsom Street Quick-Build Project
20169.teaser: Improving Safety and Comfort on Folsom
20169.summary: "a temporary improvement to traffic safety" on Folsom Street, "fully complete" at the end of 2021. The permanent redesign comes later under the Folsom-Howard Streetscape Project.

20650.name: Bayview CBTP Quick-Build Projects
20650.teaser: Improving mobility and safety in a culturally rich community
20650.summary: Quick-build changes on community-chosen Bayview streets, aimed at "improving pedestrian visibility and comfort at crossings and reducing vehicle speeds." Streets on the Vision Zero High Injury Network, such as Williams Avenue, came first.

21212.name: Anza Street Bike Lanes Project
facilities: 3.2 mi painted lane on a calm street
0.2 mi signed route on a calm street
21212.teaser: Making cycling safer in the Richmond District
added: 3.2 mi painted lane on a calm street
0.2 mi signed route on a calm street

21263.name: Golden Gate Avenue Quick-Build
21263.teaser: The Golden Gate Avenue Quick-Build project aims to improve comfort and safety for those walking and biking along Golden Gate Avenue.
21263.summary: Part of the Tenderloin quick-builds that "Stemmed from the community's demand for increased investment" in traffic safety. It installed "quick and reversible traffic safety improvements" to "improve comfort and safety for those walking and biking along Golden Gate Avenue."

21264.name: Terry Francois Boulevard Quick-Build
21264.teaser: Improving bicycling connections to the Chase Center and waterfront
21264.summary: A 2019 quick-build "protected two-way bikeway" on Terry Francois Boulevard, opened in time for the Chase Center. The page says it gives people on bikes "an attractive alternative to the busy Third Street corridor" and will become part of the San Francisco Bay Trail.

21852.name: Panhandle Social Distancing and Safety Project
21852.summary: An emergency COVID-19 response: "a parking protected bikeway on Fell Street between Baker Street and Shrader Street to provide relief to crowding and support social distancing on the Panhandle Path."

21903.name: The Embarcadero 2020 Quick-Build Projects
facilities: 0.1 mi painted lane on a calm street
21903.summary: Quick-build changes along the waterfront at Pier 35, the Ferry Terminal and the Rincon restaurant zone, completed in early 2021. They included "the corridor's first segment of a two-way protected bikeway adjacent to the promenade (between Folsom and Mission streets)".
upgraded: 0.1 mi painted lane on a calm street

22078.name: Evans Avenue Quick-Build
22078.teaser: Making biking, walking, and connecting to the 19 Polk between Cesar Chavez and 3rd streets safer.
22078.summary: SFMTA's summary: "Making biking, walking, and connecting to the 19 Polk between Cesar Chavez and 3rd streets safer." The rest of the project page could not be read.

23813.name: Battery/Sansome Quick-Build Project
23813.summary: Part of the Vision Zero Quick-Build Program, the project "assessed the feasibility of protected bikeways and implemented improvements on Battery and Sansome streets" between Market and Vallejo. It extends the earlier Sansome Battery Connections work to give a better bike connection to and from the Financial District.

24302.name: Transbay Howard Streetscape Improvement Project
24302.summary: Howard Street between 4th Street and The Embarcadero "serves as a well-traveled east-west bike route" past Moscone Center and the Transbay Terminal. The project rebuilds the streetscape along that stretch.

24436.name: Jones Street Quick-Build
24436.teaser: The Jones Street Quick-Build will build off COVID-19 response work and propose adjustable, reversible traffic safety improvements that prioritize the safety for the most vulnerable roadway users.
24436.summary: "Every street in the Tenderloin is on the city's Vision Zero High Injury Network." The quick-build made "adjustable, reversible traffic safety improvements that prioritize the safety for the most vulnerable roadway users" on Jones Street.

24472.name: Lake Merced Quick-Build Project
24472.summary: Lake Merced Boulevard from Skyline to John Muir Drive got "roadway reallocation and lane narrowing". Its two goals: traffic calming "to reduce collisions" and "safe pedestrian and bicycle connections to or along Lake Merced Boulevard".

24645.name: Golden Gate Park Access and Safety Program
24645.teaser: SFMTA and Rec Park are updating the Golden Gate Park car-free route within Golden Gate Park to: eliminate non-park traffic (cut-through), improve traffic safety, improve park access and improve the park experience for all users, especially those with high barriers to access.
24645.summary: A joint SFMTA and Recreation and Park program that made permanent "the 3-mile stretch of car-free streets in the park from Lincoln Way to Kezar Drive, including JFK Drive." Its aims: "eliminate non-park traffic (cut-through), improve traffic safety, improve park access and improve the park experience for all users".

24767.name: Lake Slow Street
24767.summary: Lake Street from 28th Avenue to Arguello Boulevard is "an important east-west connection through the Richmond neighborhood." It began as a COVID-19 Response Slow Street in April 2020 and the SFMTA Board affirmed it as a permanent Slow Street on December 6, 2022.

24778.name: Golden Gate Avenue Slow Street
24778.summary: Golden Gate Avenue is a Slow Street through North of the Panhandle, "an important connection ... to parks, schools, and the University of San Francisco." It began as a COVID-19 Response Slow Street in June 2020 and the SFMTA Board affirmed it on December 6, 2022.

26713.name: 17th Street Quick-Build
26713.teaser: Bringing quick-build traffic safety improvements to Potrero Hill
26713.summary: A quick-build on 17th Street in Potrero Hill, "unanimously approved at the March 5th SFMTA Board of Directors meeting". Construction is complete, and SFMTA will evaluate it "within 24 months of implementation."

27467.name: Frida Kahlo Way Quick-Build Project
27467.summary: The project "adds a two-way protected bikeway on the east side of Frida Kahlo Way / south side of Judson Avenue". Its purpose is to strengthen walking and biking connections between Sunnyside, Ingleside, the Ocean Avenue corridor and City College.

27602.name: 12th Avenue Slow Street
27602.summary: 12th Avenue from Lincoln Way to Lawton Street in the Inner Sunset began as a COVID-19 Response Slow Street in 2021. The SFMTA Board approved it as a permanent Slow Street on December 6, 2022.

27603.name: 23rd Avenue Slow Street
facilities: 0.3 mi signed route on a calm street
27603.summary: 23rd Avenue from Lake Street to Cabrillo Street in the Richmond began as a COVID-19 Response Slow Street in 2021. The SFMTA Board approved it as a permanent Slow Street on December 6, 2022.
upgraded: 0.3 mi signed route on a calm street

27608.name: Arlington Slow Street
27608.summary: Arlington Street from Roanoke Street to Randall Street in Glen Park began as a COVID-19 Response Slow Street in 2021. The SFMTA Board approved it as a permanent Slow Street on December 6, 2022.

27609.name: Cabrillo Slow Street
27609.summary: Cabrillo Street from 45th Avenue to 23rd Avenue in the Richmond began as a COVID-19 Response Slow Street. The SFMTA Board approved it as a permanent Slow Street on December 6, 2022.

27612.name: Clay Slow Street
27612.summary: Clay Street from Arguello Boulevard to Steiner Street in Pacific Heights began as a COVID-19 Response Slow Street in 2021. The SFMTA Board approved it as a permanent Slow Street on December 6, 2022, with targets of "Vehicle speeds at or below 15 mph" and "Vehicle volumes less than 1,000 per day".

27614.name: Hearst Avenue Slow Street
facilities: 0.8 mi signed route on a calm street
27614.summary: Hearst Avenue from Ridgewood Avenue to Baden Street in Sunnyside began as a COVID-19 Response Slow Street in 2021. The SFMTA Board approved it as a permanent Slow Street on December 6, 2022.
upgraded: 0.8 mi signed route on a calm street

27615.name: Lyon Slow Street
27615.summary: Lyon Street from Turk Street to Haight Street began as a COVID-19 Response Slow Street. The SFMTA Board approved it as a permanent Slow Street on December 6, 2022.

27618.name: Somerset Slow Street
27618.summary: Somerset Street from Silver Avenue to Woolsey Street in the Portola began as a COVID-19 Response Slow Street in 2021. The SFMTA Board approved it as a permanent Slow Street on December 6, 2022.

27619.name: Shotwell Slow Street
27619.summary: Shotwell Street, from 14th Street to Cesar Chavez, is "an important north-south connection through the Mission neighborhood." It began as a COVID-19 Response Slow Street in June 2020 and the SFMTA Board affirmed it as a permanent Slow Street on December 6, 2022.

27620.name: Sanchez Slow Street
27620.summary: Sanchez Street through Noe Valley is a Slow Street connecting destinations like the Upper Noe Recreation Center. It began as a COVID-19 Response Slow Street in June 2020 and the SFMTA Board affirmed it as a permanent Slow Street on December 6, 2022.

28173.name: SoMa Slow Streets
28173.summary: Lapu-Lapu, Rizal, Tandang Sora, Bonifacio and Mabini streets between Folsom and Harrison in SoMa began as COVID-19 Response Slow Streets in 2021. The SFMTA Board approved them as permanent Slow Streets on May 16, 2023.

28356.name: Alemany Boulevard (Ellsworth to Justin Drive/Congdon) Quick-Build Project

28710.name: 3rd Street Quick-Build Project
28710.summary: 3rd Street from the Bay Trail to Townsend Street connects Mission Bay, SoMa and Oracle Park. The project aims to "improve bike network connectivity" and deliver "transportation safety and comfort on the project corridor for all users".

28896.name: Beach Street Quick-Build Project
28896.summary: Beach Street from The Embarcadero to Polk Street in Fisherman's Wharf. The project covers "pedestrian and bicycle safety improvements, curb management changes and traffic signal retiming."

40860.name: Dr. Carlton B. Goodlett Place Quick-Build Project

45035.name: Winston Drive Quick-Build Project
45035.summary: Winston Drive from Lake Merced Boulevard to Buckingham Way gets "a separated bikeway, new transit boarding islands, pedestrian safety improvements, and parking modifications." The work is coordinated with a Public Works repaving project.
